description: The spec-library intake queue: one row per document to acquire or read, ranked by what it unblocks across the repo. Promoted verbatim (with statuses re-derived) from the 12-row markdown table in docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260804_pitch_link_stack.md, section 'Gap list, in spec-library-intake form', which itself folded in slice 1's ranked list. It lived in a lesson, so 'which document closes which gap' was answerable only by lesson archaeology; here it is a query. STATUS IS NOT STORED -- IntakeQueue.status() derives it from the library projection, so a row cannot claim to be entered while the library holds nothing it promised in `closes`. `in_pile` is stored, because data/inbox/specs/ is gitignored and invisible from a worktree; it is a human assertion about the main checkout, checked against the pile by hand.

provenance.pile: data/inbox/specs/ in the MAIN checkout C:\workspace\tolstack -- 64 entries as of 2026-08-05 (52 PDF, 8 DOCX, an XLSX, a PPTX, the tracked README.md and desktop.ini). data/inbox/specs/README.md records 42 files moved in at founding; that is a founding fact, not a current inventory, and the pile has grown since.

rows.unblocks: Nut height, slot count, slot depth for the -09 and -10 dash numbers -- the nut half of every cotter-retained joint in the repo.
rows.note: Arrived in the pile 2026-08-05 and was read the same day by handoff spec_library_v0. It supplies nut height (.188 +/-.010) and slot geometry, but NOT the thread-start-to-castellation spacing the pitch_link lesson hoped for: MS9363 does not control that, and neither does anything else (see the MS9363 family absence). The alignment remedy is procedural per JPS00094 5.9.7, capped at three washers by 5.5.3.a.

rows.unblocks: The spherical-bearing / link-eye width: the one missing term in the pitch_link stack's clamped column, and the value both of that stack's INCOMPLETE checks are written as a budget around.
rows.note: Part number UNKNOWN; candidates 215177, 214849-003, 216231-001. Now that MS9363 is in, THIS is the document standing between the repo and a complete pitch_link verdict -- it was rank 2 and is effectively rank 1 for that stack.

rows.unblocks: The .032 in flat-washer thickness band, currently a ZERO-WIDTH BAND in the pitch_link stack. The parts list has dropped even the MIN qualifier.
rows.note: Also the washer whose thickness bounds the JPS00094 5.5.3.a three-washer shim remedy, so it now has a second consumer.

rows.unblocks: Thread run-out / incomplete-thread length -- the last third of slice 1's ranked gap 1, and what its uncited 1/16 in allowance was standing in for. It is also what JPS00094 5.5.5 ("shall not engage any incomplete threads") needs to be checkable.
rows.note: PROMOTED by this session's reading. It was rank 4 as the bolt's thread spec (NAS6403 sheet 1); MS9363 sheet 2 requirement 2 invokes the SAME standard for the nut. One acquisition closes the thread form on both halves of every joint here, and it is the only named document that closes a recorded absence.

rows.unblocks: Length band -- zero-width in the pitch_link stack; slice 1 used untraced workbook limits (4.63/4.76).
Flange / barrel / chamfer -- slice 1's untraced elements 1-3.
rows.note: Balloons at sheet 5 DETAIL F, the tangential link's OTHER end (pitch_link worksheet F7).

rows.unblocks: Countersunk-washer thickness band plus the countersink geometry that the VPA stack's "under head chamfer" refers to.
Grip, length and cotter-hole position for the VPA joint's fastener.
rows.note: ENTERED 2026-08-05. The cheapest item the queue has ever held: same file as NAS6403, the dash-13 row four rows below the one the pitch_link session read. It cost one render.

Recorded so a library ingest does not assume completeness. Sheet 1's LIST OF CURRENT SHEETS names five sheets at revisions 4/2/NEW/2/3; the file in the pile holds four. The seq-1 parse event carries the same warning in its document_meta. `in_pile` is false because the SHEET is not in the pile, even though the file it belongs to is.

rows.unblocks: Whether the three 4.06 flange groups still read as they did 14 months before the assembly export.
rows.note: Only a [PRELIM 2025-MAY-22] export exists, and it is in drawing-checker's test fixtures, not in any inbox: C:\workspace\drawing-checker\tests\fixtures\drawings\[PRELIM 2025-MAY-22] 215197 A.1.pdf

Low value: a .063 in pin clears the minimum of every relevant feature -- the NAS6403 hole at .070, the NAS6404 hole at .076, and the MS9363 slot at .073. CORRECTED in review/spec_library_v0: an earlier wording here said the slot is wider than the hole so the bolt hole governs. It does not, at worst case, on either joint -- slot .073/.088 against hole .070/.080 (-09/NAS6403) and .076/.086 (-10/NAS6404) are OVERLAPPING bands, so a slot at minimum is narrower than a hole at maximum and the slot is then the governing feature. The conclusion (low value) survives; the reason did not. Pinned by tests/test_spec_library_review.py::test_neither_the_slot_nor_the_bolt_hole_governs_the_cotter_pin_outright. The MS/NASM prefix disagreement between the parts list and JPS00094 5.7.6.a is now recorded as a library criterion rather than a lesson footnote.
